summary: Australian women's captain Alyssa Healy rejected suggestions that Australia's dominance is ending after their eight-wicket Test loss to India in Mumbai, calling it "probably not even a blip". She cited unfamiliar format and conditions and recent squad change, and called for three-Test tours of India and for Tests to be part of multi-format series. Australia now turn to three ODIs and three T20s, building towards the T20 World Cup in Bangladesh late next year.
one_line: After losing the one-off Test to India by eight wickets, Alyssa Healy denies Australia's era is ending and calls for longer, multi-format Test series.
key_facts: Australia lost the one-off Test to India by eight wickets in Mumbai on Sunday, their first Test defeat to India and first loss in 11 Tests against them.
India chased down 75 in the fourth innings; Australia made 209 in their first innings and 261 in their second.
The defeat is Australia's first loss in a four-day game since January 2014.
Alyssa Healy said the loss was "probably not even a blip" and that she saw more positives than negatives.
Healy said people are "so used to seeing us winning" that they forget the team has changed a lot over the last 12 to 18 months, including the retirements of Meg Lanning and Rachael Haynes.

Australia won their fourth straight global ICC event earlier in the year at the 50-over World Cup and retained the Ashes via a drawn multi-format series in England in July, despite losing four of six white-ball matches there.
Three ODIs and three T20s against India follow; Australia are pursuing a more attacking white-ball approach, and the T20 World Cup in Bangladesh towards the end of next year is the big target.
Healy called for three-Test series in India, saying it would be a true test of both sides, though she conceded it is unlikely.
The last women's Test series of more than one match was in 2006, and India had not hosted any red-ball cricket for nine years before this summer.
Healy said the women's game is white-ball dominant and that dropping three one-day games could allow two more Tests.
The India tour is not a multi-format series, so the Test, ODIs and T20s are individual contests; Healy said this makes the Test feel "a little bit of a novelty" and "meaningless".
Australia brought the trophy used in the multi-format 2021-22 series against India but were told by authorities that system would not be used.
